title: Climbing Mount Meru: Tanzania's Underrated Mountain
excerpt: Mount Meru, at 4,566 m, is Tanzania's second-highest mountain. It is steep, beautiful, full of wildlife and much quieter than Kilimanjaro.
body:
Mount Meru rises above Arusha and is often overlooked by people heading for Kilimanjaro. That is a pity: it is one of the most beautiful climbs in East Africa.

## The basics

- Height: 4,566 m.
- Usual duration: four days (three is possible).
- Route: the Momella Route, starting inside [Arusha National Park](/national-parks/arusha-national-park/).
- Sleeping: in huts (Miriakamba and Saddle Huts).

## Wildlife on the way

Because you start in a national park, you walk with an armed ranger. You may see giraffes, buffaloes, warthogs and colobus monkeys on the first day.

## Day by day

1. Momella Gate to Miriakamba Hut, through forest and open grassland.
2. To Saddle Hut, with an afternoon walk up Little Meru (3,820 m).
3. Summit night along a narrow crater ridge to Socialist Peak, with views of Kilimanjaro at sunrise. Descent to Miriakamba.
4. Down to the gate.

## How hard is it?

The crater ridge is steep and exposed in places, but not technical. The altitude is lower than Kilimanjaro, but the climb is fairly fast.

## Before Kilimanjaro

Meru is excellent acclimatisation for Kilimanjaro. Read [why climb Meru first](/blog/mount-meru-before-kilimanjaro/).

[Plan your Meru climb](/travel-proposal/) with our partner.
